enumeration.method: Independent small-cap heading enumeration and visual comparison of all eight complete theorem statements.

checks: Eight complete main-text Theorems: 2.1–2.5, 3.1–3.2 and 4.1. Independent small-cap heading enumeration includes the locally labeled independent-variable theorem attributed to earlier work. All original/truncated branches, moment cases, covariance identities and bandwidth conditions are retained.

Nineteen source entries preserve norms, causal inputs, partial sums, coupling conventions, uniform dependence, Conditions2.1–2.4, clipping, both decay thresholds, banded quadratic blocks, the zeta1 exponent, the trend model, quantile grid, kernel and local-linear estimator. Twelve supporting passages retain necessary context separately.

Independent reconstruction confirms 45 direct uses and 72 related connections. T2.1 has no causal/dependence assumptions; T3.1 has no UI or Gaussian-coupling premise. Nonsingularity conditions and the two decay thresholds remain distinct. Theorem references import only their stated definitions or assumptions.

T2.2 second branch matches clipped covariance but targets original sums. T2.4 uses centered clipped sums only in its faster time change. T3.2 states an unconditional little-o_P bound at true second moments, importing only the numerical zeta1 definition. T4.1 applies approximation assumptions to noise Zi, with noise sums distinct from deterministic design moments.

Twelve source notes preserve the uniform-integrability comparison, reversed zeta comparison, nonmonotone second-moment times, overloaded block notation, quantile-grid endpoint inconsistency and implicit kernel conventions. Original statements are not repaired; source review does not certify proofs.

All nineteen entries have natural-language source terms, original source kinds and labels, literal selectors and complete same-paper theorem explanations. Every one of the 72 dependency paths is checked independently.

All six content JSON artifacts reproduce byte for byte. Seven retained per-paper scripts include an independent source-review check with frozen hashes, formula assertions, dependency reconstruction and schema validation.

source_notes.note: The Gaussian processes coexist with an equal-joint-law copy on a possibly enriched probability space. The original variable notation suppresses this convention. The theorem rates are o_P, not the introductory classical almost-sure KMT rate.

Clipping at n^(1/p) defines X^oplus; S^oplus additionally subtracts the clipped means. T2.2’s second branch matches Cov(X^oplus) yet compares to original S. T2.4’s faster Brownian time is the second moment of the centered clipped sum, while its slower branch uses the original sum.

Condition2.3 diverges over blocks with m_n+1 terms; Condition2.4 bounds length-l second moments below by c l. A0 and A0-prime are different formulas. T2.4 and T3.2 require neither nonsingularity condition; T3.1 only uses A>1. No implication is turned into an additional dependency.

The paper calls Condition2.2 weaker than classical uniform integrability. As printed for a fixed sequence with sup over all i, taking a=1 and reparameterizing the truncation threshold yields the same criterion. Any triangular-array interpretation would need explicit index conventions absent here.

For a dependent process the curve j↦E(S_j²) can decrease. Evaluating Brownian motion at these times is meaningful, but successive differences indexed by observations need not be independent increments. Preserve the actual time-change formulas without inferring monotonicity from the section title.

T3.1 prints D_n≤n; its sums and division implicitly require a positive integer bandwidth. Different Cp occurrences may be different constants depending only on p. At p=4 use the first polynomial branch; the second branch and mu_(4,A) require p>4.

R_j in (3.1) is a leftover linear block sum, whereas R_k in (3.3) is a centered quadratic-block partial sum. The BRV formulas initially restrict j≤ceil(n/m) then use all j≤n, and use B0 when j<m without an explicit convention. These contextual formulas are not assumed in T3.1–T3.2.

Equation(3.10) is O_(P*) conditional on observations and uses estimated possibly negative BRV times. T3.2 is an unconditional o_P existence result at true second moments. Import only the numerical zeta1 definition, not the BRV estimator or a bootstrap-conditioning assumption.

With A>1 and p>2, the printed zeta1 denominator 1+2A exceeds3, hence zeta1<zeta2. The subsequent prose prints zeta2<zeta1. The census keeps the theorem’s actual exponent and flags this reversed comparison.

The source first states t_n<t_(n+1)=1 but then sets t_i=F^-1(i/n), giving t_n=1 for its positive density. Preserve both statements; do not silently replace i/n by i/(n+1). The theorem supremum itself is on the interior interval.

The source calls K a smooth symmetric kernel with bounded support and an integrated modulus condition. It does not separately state integral K=1 or nondegeneracy of S2 S0−S1². The displayed bias beta=one-half integral u²K(u)du uses the usual normalized-kernel interpretation; do not insert unquoted assumptions into the original statement.

In the trend model Xi=mu(t_i)+Zi, the approximation assumptions apply to Zi and Si in the Gaussian increments is its noise partial sum, as resolved by (4.1). S_j(t) instead denotes deterministic kernel-weighted design moments. Q_n in T3.1 and Q_h(t) in T4.1 are unrelated reused symbols.

ambient_resolution.T2.1: Independent mean-zero variables, bounded p norms, p>2 and some gamma≥2 with the complete minimum-moment condition (2.1). Uses ordinary S_i and Brownian time E(S_i²). No causal representation, dependence norm, Condition2.2 or block variance assumption is imported. Coupling-space convention applies.
ambient_resolution.T2.2: Mean-zero causal process, Conditions2.1–2.3 and A>A0. First Gaussian covariance matches original Xi with n^(1/p)sqrt(log n) rate. Second covariance matches clipped Xi^oplus while the approximation still targets original Si at n^(1/p). Gaussian means are not separately specified in the printed theorem; no independent-increment conclusion is added.
ambient_resolution.T2.3: Conditions2.1,2.2,2.4 and the distinct A0-prime cutoff; original covariance matching and n^(1/p) rate. Does not explicitly assume Condition2.3 or use clipping.
ambient_resolution.T2.4: Conditions2.1,2.2 and A>A0 only; no nonsingularity. One Brownian approximation uses E[(S_j^oplus)²] with centered clipping and the faster rate; the original E(S_j²) time has an additional sqrt(log n).
ambient_resolution.T2.5: Inherit T2.3 assumptions: decay with A>A0-prime, truncated UI, and linear block variance lower bound. The conclusion is Brownian evaluation at original partial-sum second moments; do not import the Gaussian-process covariance-matching conclusion as a premise.
ambient_resolution.T3.1: Mean-zero causal process under Condition2.1, p>2 and A>1. Banded bounded coefficients define Q_n,V_k and centered R_k. For 2<p≤4 retain the x^(-p/2)n D_n^(p/4) mu_(p,A)^p term; for p>4 retain D_n^(p/2−1) and the exponential term with mu_(4,A)^4. No UI, nondegeneracy, Gaussian coupling or estimated-variance assumption.
ambient_resolution.T3.2: Mean-zero causal process, Condition2.1 with A>1, and Condition2.2. Zeta1=min{1,2−4/p}/(1+2A) is taken from preceding text. Brownian coupling has an unconditional little-o_P rate n^((1−A zeta1)/2)sqrt(log n). No empirical BRV input or conditional law is required.
ambient_resolution.T4.1: Trend model on the quantile design, C³ mu and f with density bounds C1,C2, and preceding kernel assumption (4.9). T2.4 assumptions apply to centered noise Zi. Si=sum_{j≤i}Zj in Yi=B(E(Si²))−B(E(S_(i−1)²)), S0=0; use the same local-linear weights to form Q_h. S_j(t) denotes distinct design moments. Interior supremum, bias constant, h→0, h^4=O(n^(1/p−1)), nh→infinity and the full error scale remain intact.

source_claim_references.scope: Import A0 only; no block-nonsingularity Condition2.3.
Conditions2.1,2.2,2.4 and A>A0-prime; no Gaussian covariance-matching conclusion is a premise.
Conditions2.1,2.2 and A>A0 for Zi; the untruncated conclusion is used to construct the Gaussian smoother. Truncation is not an additional assumption.
Numerical zeta1 formula only, not an empirical BRV premise.
Summation-by-parts and bias arguments prove the result; no proof-only weighted-variation or appendix lemma becomes a statement dependency.

review_limits: Registered arXiv:2408.02913v2 dated 7 Aug 2024, pinned by SHA-256. No substitution with another paper version.
